label: Revision-authored AQA-style practice question (original, not an AQA question)

question.context: Revision-original monthly budget exercise. A firm budgeted £80,000 income and £64,000 total expenditure. Actual income was £75,000 and actual expenditure £66,000. Variances are calculated as actual minus budget.
question.stem: Which accurately reconciles the change in budgeted profit to actual profit?

options.label: A
options.text: The £5,000 lower income is favourable, and profit rises by £7,000.

options.label: B
options.text: Total costs are £2,000 under budget, so the profit variance is £3,000 favourable.

options.label: C
options.text: Profit is £7,000 below budget (adverse), combining £5,000 lower income and £2,000 higher expenditure.

options.label: D
options.text: The profit variance is £2,000 adverse because only the change in expenditure affects profit.

option_rationale: A is incorrect because reduced income is financially adverse when other factors are held unchanged.
B is incorrect because actual costs exceed budget by £2,000 and are adverse.
C is correct because budgeted profit is £80,000 − £64,000 = £16,000, actual profit is £75,000 − £66,000 = £9,000, and £9,000 − £16,000 = −£7,000 adverse.
D is incorrect because the £5,000 shortfall in income also reduces profit.
mark_scheme.model_answer: C. Budgeted profit £16,000; actual profit £9,000; profit variance −£7,000 adverse. This combines −£5,000 income with +£2,000 cost (actual minus budget).
